subject: Pharmacology
concept: Drug treatment of leukemias and lymphomas uses cytotoxic, targeted and immune-based therapies selected according to disease biology.

content.definition: Anticancer pharmacology includes agents that inhibit malignant-cell proliferation or exploit disease-specific molecular or immune vulnerabilities.
content.explanation: Teaching groups include antimetabolites, alkylating agents, anthracyclines, vinca alkaloids, corticosteroids, monoclonal antibodies and molecularly targeted inhibitors.
content.mechanism: Different classes interfere with DNA synthesis, DNA integrity, mitosis, signaling pathways or immune recognition.
content.clinical_relevance: Modern treatment is increasingly guided by molecular and immunophenotypic classification.
content.treatment: Regimens are malignancy-specific and should follow current oncology/hematology guidance.
effects: Myelosuppression and infection risk are important class effects.
Organ-specific toxicity varies by drug class.
Targeted and immune therapies have characteristic mechanism-related adverse effects.
high_yield: Anticancer therapy in hematology is disease- and biology-specific.
Targeted therapy acts on defined molecular pathways.
Monoclonal antibodies can target lineage-associated surface antigens.

yemen_context.relevance: Core Hematology block pharmacology topic; access to advanced targeted agents varies by setting.
yemen_context.evidence: General evidence; no local formulary asserted.

review_notes: Original educational synthesis based on major hematology/oncology references.
